claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-0:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 17: "| Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau |". No line in the file gives a reason for the delay.

Lines 31-33: "Việc "Ngừng gửi thông báo" chưa xong nên không được trình diễn — chưa xong thì chưa tính, dù đã viết gần hết code." Consistent with Scrum Guide 2020: "If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review."

Lines 37-39: "Làm tốt: viết tiêu chí chấp nhận trước khi code…", "Cần sửa: nhận việc phụ thuộc vào một người duy nhất.", "Hành động cho sprint sau: mỗi việc lớn hơn 3 điểm phải có hai người đọc code." None mentions an estimate. Both quoted code blocks match the file character-for-character.

Scrum Guide 2020 gives the retrospective a different job: "The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness"; "The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done." The Sprint Review also looks back: "The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint". Nothing makes the retrospective the only place to compare a guess with reality.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Only after the work is actually done can anyone see how the guess compared with reality. The retrospective, the meeting that ends the sprint where the team looks at how it worked, is a good place to talk about it. An item that did not finish is information for that conversation, not proof that someone broke a promise.

claim_verdicts.evidence: No official source in versions.yaml covers this behavioural effect; the Scrum Guide 2020 is silent on estimate inflation. As an opinion it is acceptable only if hedged; the lesson states it as certainty ("Either way, the numbers stop describing the work, and planning gets worse, not better.").
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: People who are held to their guesses can start protecting themselves: they may give bigger numbers next time, or call work "done" when it is not, so the sprint looks as planned. Either way, the numbers can stop describing the work, which makes planning harder, not easier.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: estimates are made at planning. Scrum Guide 2020 puts sizing in Product Backlog refinement, an ongoing activity ("Product Backlog refinement is the act of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items…"; "The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing."). The same assertion is repeated in q1's `correct` explanation ("An estimate is made at planning").
issues.quote: It is made at planning, with what the team knows at that moment.
issues.fix: Change to: "It is made before the work starts, with what the team knows at that moment." In q1 explanation.correct (en/vi) replace "made at planning, before anyone starts" with "made before anyone starts". Optionally relabel the diagram node P to "before starting: estimate".

issues.text: Claim 4 rephrased: the retrospective is not the only place, nor defined by Scrum 2020 as the place, where a guess is compared with reality; its stated purpose is improving quality and effectiveness, and the Sprint Review inspects the outcome. Summary line 4 repeats the overstatement with "Only the retrospective".
issues.quote: That is the job of the retrospective
issues.fix: Replace section 4 paragraph 3 with claim 4's suggested_text. Summary line 4 → "Only after the work is done can a guess be compared with what really happened; the retrospective is a good place to do it."

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and at odds with Scrum Guide 2020, which says an unfinished item "returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration" — not that it moves into the next sprint. The lesson presents moving to the next sprint as what carry over means in general; only the Sprint 14 file says "chuyển sprint sau".
issues.quote: carry over — moving an unfinished item into the next sprint instead of counting it as done.
issues.fix: Define: "carry over — putting an unfinished item back in the backlog, often to pick up in the next sprint, instead of counting it as done." Add a claim (kind fact, version_key scrum) citing the Scrum Guide sentence.

issues.text: Unlisted claim with no version: the lesson states Scrum event facts (retrospective is "the meeting at the end of the sprint"; unfinished work is not shown at the sprint review) while versions_used is []. Sibling lessons relative-estimation and scrum-from-junior-seat declare [scrum]. The facts themselves hold in Scrum Guide 2020 ("The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint.").
issues.quote: the retrospective, the meeting at the end of the sprint where the team looks at how it worked
issues.fix: Set versions_used: [scrum] in front matter. Add a meta claim (kind fact, version_key scrum, section 4) for "the retrospective concludes the sprint" with source_hint scrumguides.org Sprint Retrospective.
